newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria seeking to restructure Paris Club debt.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria seeking to restructure Paris Club debt.

text.p: Bulgaria is seeking to restructure its $2 billion debt to the Paris Club of official creditors and plans to include local commercial banks' debts to institutions based in countries who are members of the club, Bulbank executive director Chavdar Kanchev told Reuters.

"We will seek to restructure Bulgaria's debt to the Paris Club under conditions similar to those agreed by Poland and Russia," said Kanchev ,who is also a member of the Financial Stabilisation Council set up by the interim government to map financial policy and negotiate with foreign lenders.
Poland had agreed a 50 percent reduction of its debt to the Paris Club and Russia had rescheduled its dues over 25-year peroid.
Government debts accumulated under the communist regime which collapsed in 1989 were included in the balance sheet of Bulbank then known as the Bulgarian Foreign Trade Bank.

Kanchev said that the government is prepared to include in the future restructuring package foreign debts owed by local commercial banks to institutions based in member-states of the Paris Club, which so far have not been rescheduled.
One of them is Economic Bank's debt of around $170 million. The bank was put into receivership on September 23 year.
Bulgaria's interim Prime Minister Stefan Sofianski last month sent a letter to the Paris Club seeking to rollover up to $50 million of this year's non-rescheduled payments.
Bulgaria has so far paid these amounts regularly, but an economic crisis has depleted its reserves.
Under three agreements to reschedule a $1.2 billion debt owed to the Paris Club by 1995, Bulgaria is due to pay official creditors $126 million this year.
A part of the debt of both state banks - Economic bank and Mineralbank might be considered as a state debt, bankers said. -- Sofia Newsroom, 359-2-84561
